title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 260 (Omitted — sick companies / Chapter XIX)

content.overview: Section 260 formed part of Chapter XIX (sections 253 to 269) on revival and rehabilitation of sick companies. That chapter has been omitted. Sick-company determination and revival under Chapter XIX are not current law. Corporate debt default and insolvency resolution for corporate persons are governed by the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, before the National Company Law Tribunal as adjudicating authority.
content.glance: s. 260 omitted with Chapter XIX (sick-company revival); not current procedure; use IBC for corporate insolvency and liquidation.
content.study: Section 260 was part of Chapter XIX on revival and rehabilitation of sick companies. Sections 253 to 269 were omitted; they are not the current route for corporate distress. Current corporate insolvency resolution and liquidation of corporate persons is under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016. A study answer that treats s. 260 as available current procedure is wrong. The topic is retained so the omitted number is not mistaken for a gap in the Act. Related omitted numbers in the same chapter (e.g. s. 253) carry the same pointer.

sections.heading: Omission
sections.body: Section 260 and Chapter XIX (ss. 253–269) on sick-company revival have been omitted and are not in force.

sections.heading: Current Law
sections.body: Corporate insolvency resolution and liquidation for debt default are under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, before the NCLT.

sections.heading: Study Note
sections.body: Do not plead omitted Chapter XIX as current procedure. Name the IBC route where corporate distress is in issue.

examples.title: Old reference
examples.body: A draft petition invoking s. 260 or Chapter XIX sick-company revival cannot be filed as current law.

examples.title: Current forum
examples.body: A financial creditor seeking resolution of corporate debt default proceeds under the IBC before the NCLT, not under omitted s. 260.

hypotheticals.question: Can a creditor still move under s. 260 for sick-company revival?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 260 and Chapter XIX have been omitted. Corporate insolvency is under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016.

distinctions.title: Omitted sick-company route (s. 260 / Chapter XIX) vs IBC
distinctions.left: Omitted Chapter XIX revival and rehabilitation — not current law
distinctions.right: IBC corporate insolvency resolution and liquidation before NCLT

misconceptions.trap: Section 260 is still available for declaring a company sick and ordering revival.
misconceptions.correction: Section 260 and Chapter XIX have been omitted. Debt default and corporate insolvency are under the IBC.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 260 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. State that s. 260 / Chapter XIX is omitted. II. Name the IBC route for corporate insolvency. III. Conclude that the omitted section is not current procedure.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Omission status; current IBC path; precise relief under current law.
